summary.text: A 24-year-old woman with systemic lupus erythematosus diagnosed in 2019, treated with prednisolone and hydroxychloroquine with a controlled disease course, presented three years later with shortness of breath, diffuse abdominal pain and abdominal distension. Examination showed decreased breath sounds bilaterally, tenderness all over the abdomen and shifting dullness.

Chest X-ray showed bilateral pleural effusion, ultrasound showed severe free fluid, and echocardiography showed an ejection fraction of 70% with mild-to-moderate pericardial effusion. Laboratory results included low hemoglobin, elevated creatinine and urea nitrogen, raised inflammatory markers and CA-125 of 198 U/mL. Duplex ultrasonography was normal, CT showed no cancerous lesions, and ascitic fluid culture and tuberculosis PCR showed no infection, with no tumor cells found.

Intravenous furosemide for two days did not improve the ascites. She was diagnosed with pseudo-pseudo Meigs syndrome with ascites and pleural effusion; furosemide was stopped and intravenous methylprednisolone 500 mg daily for three days gave gradual improvement, followed by discharge on oral prednisone 50 mg daily for one month. A month later she showed marked improvement, with no ascites or pleural effusion on repeated investigations.
